name: Tennessee

code.name: Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 2 (Elections); the official Tennessee Code Unannotated is published for the State by LexisNexis

ctas-tie.citation: University of Tennessee Institute for Public Service, County Technical Assistance Service (CTAS), e-Li, 'Tie Votes' (CTAS-865), citing T.C.A. 2-8-111 and 2-8-114
ctas-tie.note: A plain page of a state university agency that advises counties: the agency's guide to the Code, a lower grade than the statute. Read once with curl (HTTP 200, 2026-11-07T08:12Z). It gives the rule in a sentence and cites the sections; the Code's own words were not read.

ties.applies_to: a tie in a general election involving a single county or a part of a county, or in a municipal election
ties.steps: the county legislative body (for a county election) or the municipal legislative body (for a municipal election) casts the deciding vote, or may call a runoff
ties.who: the county or municipal legislative body

sources.quote: Elections involving a single county or a part of a county - county legislative body (or the legislative body may call for a runoff);
Municipal elections - municipal legislative body (or the legislative body may call for a runoff);

ties.note: The guide's words, citing T.C.A. 2-8-111. 'A runoff election' is the body's option, not the rule.

ties.applies_to: a general election for a U.S. House seat (the guide says 'U.S. Congress' and sets the U.S. Senator apart)
ties.steps: the governor casts the deciding vote
ties.note: The guide lists 'U.S. Congress' and then 'except U.S. Senator' under the last item, so the House reading is [inferred] from its own separate rule for the Senator.

ties.applies_to: a general election for U.S. Senator
ties.steps: the election is void and the governor orders a special election

sources.quote: An election for U.S. Senator is void if it results in a tie, and the governor is to order a special election.

ties.steps: the General Assembly casts the deciding vote

ties.applies_to: a general election for any other office except U.S. Senator that the guide does not list (the other statewide offices and the General Assembly are read to fall here)
ties.steps: the state election commission casts the deciding vote

sources.quote: Any other election except U.S. Senator (see below) - state election commission.

ties.note: The guide says 'any other election'; that this covers statewide offices other than governor and the General Assembly is the reader's reading [inferred].

ties.steps: the tie is broken according to the rules of the political party

sources.quote: If a tie vote occurs in a primary election, the tie shall be broken according to the rules of the political party.

ties.note: The guide cites T.C.A. 2-8-114. The parties' rules were not read.

ties.steps: not read: the guide does not mention them
ties.note: The guide is a short page; the Code was not reachable.
